title: LEAVEN: THE ROOT OF BITTERNESS PART 2

sense.text:
“I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one.” The wicked one is Satan, and this whole lesson is about overcoming the wicked one.

The root of bitterness is one of the devices Satan uses to destroy brothers and take them out of the truth. Lust and fornication, and bitterness: those are the two rampant sins among our people, the two things that destroy brothers and sisters and make them leave the truth. Somebody did something to you and you didn’t deal with it right, or you felt offended, or Satan played with your mind; it could even be from correction. Bitterness rose up in you and you fell out of the truth.

The one who plays on that bitterness, who whispers things in your mind that are not there to make it grow, is Satan. So you have to learn how to fight Satan: how to fight that root of bitterness, how to see the seed when it is trying to be planted in you, and how to get rid of it if it is already there. It is leaven, and it will stop you from getting the kingdom of heaven. The young men back then knew how to fight Satan; today, brothers, you have to learn how to fight this war we are in and where the war begins.

precepts.why:
“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.” Satan’s job is to devour you, to destroy you. But the young men of 1 John 2:14 had overcome the wicked one, so he can be fought.

“Be sober” means be clear-minded. “Be vigilant” means you are always aware: you are fighting a battle, so you are always looking, paying attention, always looking for Satan, because he comes from different angles. “Your adversary the devil” is the spiritual demon Satan.

How does he devour you with the root of bitterness? The same way he did it to Cain. When Cain’s sacrifice was not accepted, Satan put that hatred spirit on him and played on it; Cain ended up hating his brother, became a servant of Satan, and killed his brother, because he gave in to the root of bitterness and envy.

So be vigilant: pay attention to the things people say to you, because Satan can use people to plant evil seeds in your mind.

“So fight I, not as one that beateth the air.” Fighting Satan is not like swinging in the air. “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection”: the way you fight Satan is by controlling your body and controlling your mind.

When those evil thoughts come in your mind, when the root of bitterness tries to rise up in you, you fight it off, you shake it off, you don’t listen to it. That thought that comes to your mind, that sister don’t like you, that person said this about you, is the seed. When somebody comes and tells you so-and-so said so-and-so about you, they are planting a seed, and now you are going to become bitter toward that person. Ask them: and what did you say? Did you correct that person? If not, you don’t want to hear it; you were supposed to correct them. And if they feel comfortable bringing that to you about somebody, you have to watch them sideways too. Satan can jump in a brother or sister and send them gossiping to plant an evil seed against another brother or sister in the truth.

The fight is not physical but spiritual, and spiritual means it is in your mind. Every sin every last one of us commits starts in the mind. If you can kill the root of bitterness in your mind when that seed tries creeping in, it will not manifest itself and it will not bear root.

That is why a brother who reaches out is to be respected. A brother once asked if the Deacon had a problem with him, because he said shalom at the new moon and felt ignored, when the Deacon’s mind was far away meditating and he never noticed. Satan could have played with that brother’s head and grown bitterness for no reason; instead he came straight and it was settled. That is how you get rid of bitterness: you sit there thinking a person is moving a certain way or did you wrong, when the person is not aware of anything running through your mind. Satan whispers in your mind and makes you believe things that are not there.

And if anybody comes and tells you the Deacon said this about you, don’t believe them: the Deacon will tell you to your face.

sense.text:
“It is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.” If you do things you are not supposed to do, it is not you, but sin that lies in you.

A lot of brothers and sisters went off because of the root of bitterness, because they don’t know how to fight it or how to deal with the evil thoughts that keep coming to their mind. When Satan attacks, he keeps putting thoughts in your mind and you keep listening to him.

“When I would do good, evil is present with me.” Evil is present with all of us all the time. Here you are repenting and trying to do good, and here comes Satan, the roaring lion seeking whom he may devour, causing problems and tempting you in different ways. When you will do good, Satan is always there.
“For I delight in the law of God after the inward man.” The way we delight in the law of God is from the inward man, meaning in your mind: something you cannot see, the inner you.

“But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind.” There is something in you that wars against your mind. You want to do good, you want to do right, but something is telling you evil all the time. That is Satan. The thoughts warring against your mind are Satan.

Somebody says something to you and it triggers your mind: who the hell that person think they are, who he think he talking to, I could be this dude mother. Some of the officers are disrespectful to the people at times, and when that is found out their rank will be taken. But even if the brother was wrong in how he dealt with you, that is Satan whispering all types of things, until all of a sudden your mind says, I don’t like him. You still cannot entertain those evil thoughts, because they turn into bitterness. Everybody here is trying to become perfect and people are not perfect; people will offend you. Either go to that person and fix it, but you cannot sit there and become bitter and hateful.

Brothers are not supposed to stop talking to a brother because of a sister. That is weird, that is bitterness. Sisters do it too: two sisters were cool, both liked the same brother, he chose one, and now they stop talking. That is bitterness and that is fake. We cannot rule like that. If that brother is for you, he is for you. Brothers who stop talking to each other because of a woman, I ain’t talking to you because you talking to the sister and I like the sister first, that thing is so fake; that is fake and phony, mark them, and they had better repent.

There is a war that goes on in every last one of our minds, the war between good and evil: you want to do good and Satan is whispering in your ear to do evil. “And bringing me into captivity to the law of sin”: that is what it is trying to do, bring you into captivity, the captivity of sin, the captivity of bitterness.

“O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God.” That is how we serve God and how we fight Satan: with the mind. Everything starts with your mind, and your mind controls your thoughts.

When evil thoughts come to your mind concerning your brother or your sister, you have to shake it off. The root of bitterness will destroy you. Don’t play with bitterness, don’t play with hatred, don’t play with envy. When these things start creeping up in you, shake it off.

precepts.why:
The Most High brings people together. The angel tells the young man of Raguel’s “one only daughter, named Sara; I will speak for her, that she may be given thee for a wife. For to thee doth the right of her appertain, seeing thou only art of her kindred.” And the angel says: “fear not, for she is appointed unto thee from the beginning.”

She was appointed unto you from the beginning: ever since the beginning, that is your wife. God says in the beginning she was yours. So God brings people together.

So brothers and sisters, do not develop bitterness and hatred toward each other over who is talking to who. Don’t say, I don’t like that brother, I stopped talking to him because he talking to the sister and he know I like the sister first. Don’t come in here with that kind of fakeness. You are supposed to be happy for the brother. Same for you sisters: don’t be bitter because another sister is talking to a brother you liked; be happy for her. That bitterness is going to change you, and it is just a matter of time before you leave the body.

“But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost.” The war always starts in the mind, and the one who puts these things in your mind is Satan. The young men overcame the wicked one, and overcoming Satan starts with the mind.

Satan came in that brother’s mind and said, you don’t have to tell the apostles how much you really sold the land for. That thought came in his mind, and he could have said, no, I can’t think like that. But he gave in to the thought, and then he went and lied to the apostles.

That is how Satan attacks: in your mind, whispering things. If you are not careful and vigilant and paying attention to your thoughts, you will defile yourself and get caught up in sin.

sense.text: An example of the root of bitterness: King David and Saul. David came back from killing the Philistines, and “the women came out of all cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet king Saul.”

“And the women answered one another as they played, and said, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.” They answered each other; it was a song. One would sing, Saul killed a thousand, and the next, David killed ten thousand, back and forth, enjoying themselves.

But Satan was there too. Satan knew that would get to Saul, and Satan went to Saul: you hear that, man? You hear that?

“And Saul was very wroth”: he got angry. Remember the Lord asking Cain, why are you angry? Did David kill ten thousand? Yes, he did. The Lord was fighting with David; David was another level of warrior.

“They have ascribed unto David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed but thousands: and what can he have more but the kingdom?” He wants my position. That is Satan whispering those things in his mind, and Saul allowed those thoughts to enter: David wants my position, the people love David, they are saying he is better than me. Satan in his ear: watch him, he thinks he is better than you. And Saul listened to him.

“And Saul eyed David from that day and forward.” He envied David and became bitter toward David after that; he started watching him sideways, that boy wants my position.

Why did that happen to Saul? Because Saul entertained Satan. Satan used that situation to put an evil spirit on Saul, the spirit of envy. Instead of Saul saying, that is good for me, let David go kill everybody for me, or David is a godly man, he does not want my position, Satan came and played with his mind. That is how Satan attacks.
This is when Saul was hunting David to kill him. Here is what caused Saul to think that way, and how David dealt with it, a lesson all of us can learn from.
Abishai answered David, “I will go down with thee.”
Saul lay sleeping in the trench with his spear at his bolster, “but Abner and the people lay round about him.” Abner was the top warrior in Israel at that time.

“God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day.” The enemy was King Saul. Saul was hunting David because Saul was dealing with bitterness and envy and hatred. “Now therefore let me smite him, I pray thee, with the spear even to the earth at once”: let me kill him right now. But see how David dealt with it.

“Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the Lord’s anointed, and be guiltless?” Saul was anointed by the Lord to be king, and David understood he could not kill one of God’s anointed. That is the kind of love David had toward his people.

“As the Lord liveth, the Lord shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish.” The Lord is the one who is going to deal with Saul if he does not change; he might go to war and somebody else might kill him, but David did not want that blood on his hands.

That is the same state of mind we all have to have. Was Saul doing David wrong? Yes, he was hunting him to kill him. But you don’t have to do evil back to somebody because they are dealing wrong with you. Sometimes it is good to leave it in God’s hands, and that is what King David did.

David took the spear and the cruse of water, “for they were all asleep; because a deep sleep from the Lord was fallen upon them.” He went to the other side and stood on the top of a hill afar off, and cried to Abner. Abner was the top warrior of the tribe of Benjamin, supposed to protect the king; but David went down there and could have killed Saul, and he did not.

“Wherefore then hast thou not kept thy lord the king?” “As the Lord liveth, ye are worthy to die, because ye have not kept your master, the Lord’s anointed.” David told Abner he was worthy of death, because somebody could have killed the king and he was supposed to be protecting him. “And now see where the king’s spear is”: look for the spear and the water and see if you can find it.
“Is this thy voice, my son David?” Saul dealt with David as a son, but the jealousy was still there. Satan was messing with his mind, making him think David wanted his position.
“Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in mine hand?” Why are you pursuing me and trying to kill me? What wrong have I done to you?

“If the Lord have stirred thee up against me, let him accept an offering.” Sometimes the Lord can put a spirit on somebody to deal wrongfully with you, to see how you operate, to try you. How you deal with it tells whether you get the kingdom or not. If you become bitter and deal with it wrong, you lose the kingdom; that person can say, I didn’t know, I’m sorry, and the Lord forgives that brother, but you, because you became bitter and never dealt with it right, lost the kingdom. That is how David thought: later, when that man was cursing David and calling him a bloody man, David said leave him alone, it is the Lord telling him to curse me. That man was not right, and in the end he was killed.

“But if they be the children of men, cursed be they before the Lord.” David understood that Saul had men around him whispering in his ears: David thinks he is better than you, David wants the kingdom, he wants to kill you. Satan was in those men, and it was all to defile King Saul. Saul fed into it; he could have said, I don’t want to hear that, David is a man of God, he will never do that to me. But he listened and played into it.

That is why you had better be vigilant. If somebody comes and whispers evil to you: I don’t want to hear that. Why are you saying this to me, do you want me to hate that person? Did you correct them when they said that? That is the posture to take. People in the body have spread evil, even about the Deacon, and brothers ended up hating him over things he never said. A few years back there were wormwood, worm-tongue brothers whispering and murmuring. Find one murmurer, one bitter brother who cannot stand leadership because he got corrected, and everybody buddy-buddy in that circle is defiled, because they all have the same spirit; if you separate yourself from these, you will be a vessel to honour. Bitter brothers are given rope to see who gravitates to them, because whoever does is not spiritual either.

“For they have driven me out this day from abiding in the inheritance of the Lord, saying, Go, serve other gods.” They drove off King David: go serve other gods, we don’t want you in Israel.
“For the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.” David is saying, I am nothing; he is humbling himself.

“Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David.” Saul was catching himself, because David hit a nerve: anybody telling you I want to kill you or take the kingdom, cursed is that person. Saul knew a couple of people were probably telling him that, and David could have killed him right then and did not.

The Lord was proving David: an evil spirit from the Lord was on Saul, and people around him were messing with his head too, and Saul kept catching himself. Sometimes Satan jumps on people and they do evil to you, and afterward they say, why would I do that, I’m sorry. When somebody comes at you sideways, it is not necessarily the person in front of you that you are fighting; it is Satan in them. Even in marriage: Satan will jump on a brother and he will say evil things to his wife, and, sister, you have to realize that is not your husband, that is Satan you are dealing with. When Satan entered into Job’s wife she said, curse God and die; and Job said, why are you acting like one of these simple women? It was not her Job was dealing with; Satan entered into her and was speaking.

“For the Lord delivered thee into my hand to day, but I would not stretch forth mine hand against the Lord’s anointed.” “So let my life be much set by in the eyes of the Lord, and let him deliver me out of all tribulation.” That is what you want, brothers: for the Lord to deliver you out of tribulation and what you are going through, and not to take vengeance into your own hands. That is what David understood.

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him. Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people.”

This is what David understood. David had love for his brother and did not want to take vengeance. Bearing a grudge is where bitterness and all of that comes from. Even though David could have killed Saul, he did not take vengeance, even though Saul was bitter against him and wanted him dead, and Saul was bitter because Satan was messing with his mind.

“He that revengeth shall find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.” If you take vengeance you are going to find vengeance from the Lord. If David had taken vengeance, he would have found vengeance from the Lord. You cannot be talking about wanting vengeance; the scripture says do not avenge or bear any grudge against the children of thy people.

“Forgive thy neighbour the hurt that he hath done unto thee.” We will do things to hurt each other from time to time; your wife will hurt you, sisters, your husband will hurt you. But you have to forgive your neighbour the hurt. King David forgave Saul for trying to kill him; he could have taken vengeance on him and he never did. That is the passion we have to have.

Why does it say the hurt? Because it hurts, and you don’t really want to forgive. It is hard; sometimes people do things where you don’t even want to see them anymore. But you have to do what God says and get rid of that pride, because if you don’t forgive, it turns into bitterness. Forgive your spouse, your neighbour, your brother, however they hurt you, once they come and say, I’m sorry.

“So shall thy sins also be forgiven when thou prayest.” That is the only time your sins are going to be forgiven: if you are able to forgive. Not just the small things you want to forgive, but the stuff that really hurt.

“One man beareth hatred against another, and doth he seek pardon from the Lord?” You are bearing hatred toward someone and coming to God, talking about serving God: you are fake and you are phony. Bearing grudges and bitterness toward your spouse while saying you love God makes you phony. And brothers who deal evil with their wives until the marriage falls apart will be put out.

sense.text:
“Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them.” The root of bitterness is not just congregational; it also goes into how a brother deals with his wife. Bishop was very serious about marriage and how brothers deal with their wives and rule in their house, and every leader who deals with counsel needs to understand this.

Women can do things where you end up bitter toward them, and where there is bitterness in the marriage there is no love, there is a separation. Couples come to counsel over and over and cannot fix it, and then the sister leaves: she can’t take it anymore. A brother bitter toward his wife forces her to leave, with the thought in his mind, why the hell she ain’t go commit adultery so I could divorce her and marry another sister. God can read your mind and hears those thoughts, and you are not going to last in here. That thought should never come to your mind; that is bitterness. You and your wife are one flesh, you are supposed to try to save her and love her like you love yourself. If she fell back into the world because of you being evil, you have to go too, and brothers will not trust you. Let him repent and change.

This was said because it happens a lot among our people: some sisters are bitter toward their husbands and some brothers toward their wives, and there are levels to it. The low form: you come home planning to get some later, she falls asleep, and you are wanting it out of her like, God damn. In the morning she says, hey babe, and it is, don’t talk to me, I wanted some last night. That can be fixed easy. But the other kind is really hatred, where a brother hates his wife; that is the bitterness that destroys marriages, and if it is in you, examine yourself.

Women mostly become bitter from correction, so sisters have to work on that bitterness too. Listen to your husband in all things, even if he is wrong. Be like Sarah: Abraham was wrong and she still listened to him. Don’t try to prove he is wrong; be quiet, go to the Lord and pray.

This is how to fight the root of bitterness. “Charity suffereth long”: if you really love your brother, your wife, your spouse, you are going to suffer long, endure the bull crap; you are patient. “And is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up.”

“Is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil.” When Satan puts evil thoughts in your mind about someone else, charity is not going to think evil. Say, no, I am not going to think evil about that person; when that thought comes, shake it off. Repeat it over and over, even if people think you are crazy: charity thinketh no evil. Somebody said something? That person probably didn’t mean it like that. Charity thinketh no evil.

When something happens, don’t be quick to think evil. If you have charity, you will not be quick to think evil of that person; sometimes that person did not say it, and sometimes it is a slander.

“Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.” To wink at ignorance means sometimes people say dumb stupid stuff. Sometimes it is immaturity, the person has not grown, and they probably didn’t mean it that way. For the root of bitterness not to build up in you, sometimes you just have to wink at it: that person just doesn’t know. Don’t take it seriously.

When people do evil things to you, wink at it; don’t let bitterness rise up inside you. Everybody here is not perfect and people will get on your nerves. We are trying to become perfect, with people from different walks of life, so it is all about applying the law of loving each other as we love ourselves and getting rid of bitterness.

“Abstain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins: for a furious man will kindle strife.” Strife is arguing: the arguing and the bitterness, going back and forth. Brothers and sisters who keep arguing and striving all the damn time have something evil in them. Abstaining from strife is how you diminish your sins.

“Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it.” You hear somebody said something about you: go and admonish that person, correct and warn them, because sometimes the person never said it. It could be Satan messing with you, or somebody slandering or trying to cause confusion. “And if he have done it, that he do it no more”: if he did you wrong, tell him, don’t do that again.

“Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again.” That is how to get rid of the root of bitterness: you hear something, or think somebody did something to you, go and admonish that person. Don’t hold on to it inside, because Satan can play with that and it can turn into the root of bitterness. If they did say something evil about you, tell them not to say it again; if they say they are sorry, forgive them, forget about it, and don’t hold on to it.

“Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.” A lot of times when somebody comes and says, this person said this and that, that person doesn’t like you, it is slander. It is Satan. Don’t believe everything you hear, because Satan is real.

“There is one that slippeth in his speech, but not from his heart.” Brothers and sisters slip in their speech and say something offensive, and you think, why did that person say that to me? But they did not mean to hurt or offend you; they are just offensive when they speak. If you take it inside, you become bitter toward a person who meant nothing by it. God read their mind, but your mind took it as evil.

“And who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?” Every one of us is going to offend from time to time with our tongue, saying something someone does not like even when we did not mean it in a bad way.

“Admonish thy neighbour before thou threaten him”: warn your neighbour before you go threatening him, instead of wanting to fight somebody. “And not being angry, give place to the law of the most High”: you cannot be angry; always give place to the law of the Most High, meaning you go to that person and try to fix it.

“So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.” God wants us to forgive from the heart: it has to be real, not fake. Some say, I forgive you, then go to the next city, you know what that sister did to me? You never really forgave. God can read your heart and tell if you really forgave someone.

That goes for spouses too. When the scripture says love thy neighbour, your neighbour is your spouse, your brother, your sister, the person you are married to; love them as yourself. Sisters, if your husband did something to you, forgive him from your heart; brothers, the same with your wife. Otherwise Satan can use it, and bitterness rises up in your mind.

Another way to deal with bitterness. “Love your enemies”: Saul was David’s enemy, and David still loved him. That is an example of how to get rid of bitterness.

“Bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you.” Some sisters say, that person don’t like me. So what if they don’t? Some of you are mean, and that is why.

“And pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you.” This is how you get rid of bitterness: if somebody is dealing evil with you, don’t entertain it; pray for them. God, take that spirit away from this sister, help her, make her stop dealing like that with me. Lord, take that mean spirit away from my husband. Instead of saying, my husband is wicked, pray for him. Your enemy could even be your own spouse, when Satan jumps on them and they are being evil.

Instead of trying to take vengeance and avenge yourself, leave it to the Lord. Instead of sitting there with bitterness and hatred toward each other, approach that person and fix it; if he does not want to fix it, leave it to the Lord. Wink at ignorance, pray for that person, charity thinketh no evil. That is how you really purge the leaven out of your spirit.
